questions.stem: What happens to the boiling points of noble gases going down Group 0?
questions.explanation: Boiling points increase going down Group 0. Larger atoms have more electrons, which creates stronger London dispersion forces (van der Waals forces) between atoms. More energy is needed to overcome these stronger forces, so boiling points rise from helium (-269 degrees C) to radon (-62 degrees C).

questions.stem: Why is helium used in airships instead of hydrogen?

options.text: Helium is non-flammable, making it much safer

questions.explanation: Helium is used instead of hydrogen because it is non-flammable. Both gases are lighter than air and can lift airships, but hydrogen is highly flammable and can explode. Helium is a noble gas and will not react with oxygen, making it much safer.
